Arrange the records in ascending alphabetical order. R1, R2, and so on are fixed record labels, not answer-option letters. Ignore letter case. Compare word by word, comparing letters within each word. If one word or complete name is an exact prefix of another, put the shorter one first. 

R1: Folder
R2: Basket
R3: Stapler
R4: Envelope

Which sequence gives the correct filing order?
explanation: The first letters give B, E, F, S: Basket, Envelope, Folder, Stapler. The correct order is R2-R4-R1-R3.

stem:
Arrange the records in ascending alphabetical order. R1, R2, and so on are fixed record labels, not answer-option letters. Ignore letter case. Each record is written Surname, Given name. Compare surnames first, then given names if surnames tie. Compare word by word, comparing letters within each word. If one word or complete name is an exact prefix of another, put the shorter one first. 

R1: Lim, Nora
R2: Garcia, Leo
R3: Ramos, Iris
R4: Cruz, Emil

Which sequence gives the correct filing order?
explanation: Compare surnames, not given names: Cruz, Garcia, Lim, Ramos. No surname tie requires a given-name comparison. Sorting by the given names Emil, Iris, Leo, Nora would instead produce R4-R3-R2-R1, which violates the surname-first rule. The correct order is R4-R2-R1-R3.

Compare word by word, comparing letters within each word. If one word or complete name is an exact prefix of another, put the shorter one first. Ignore periods, but do not expand abbreviations: St. is filed as St, not as Saint.

R1: Saint Alder Clinic
R2: St. Alder Clinic
R3: St. Alden Clinic
R4: Saint Alden Clinic
R5: St. Alder College

Which sequence gives the correct filing order?
explanation: Saint comes before St because a precedes t. Within each first-word group, Alden precedes Alder because n precedes r. For the two St Alder entries, Clinic precedes College because l precedes o after C. The correct order is R4-R1-R3-R2-R5.

stem:
Arrange the records in ascending alphabetical order. R1, R2, and so on are fixed record labels, not answer-option letters. Ignore letter case. Before comparing names, omit a leading A, An, or The and remove apostrophes and hyphens without adding spaces. Keep all other spaces as word boundaries. Compare the resulting names word by word, comparing letters within each word. If one word or complete name is an exact prefix of another, put the shorter one first.

R1: The Brook-side Art Center
R2: Brookside Arts Center
R3: Brookside Art Centre
R4: A Brookside Art Center Annex
R5: Brook's Art Center
R6: The Brookside Art Center Archives

Which sequence gives the correct filing order?
explanation: First normalize the names as directed. R5 begins Brooks, an exact shorter prefix of Brookside, so it comes first. Among the Brookside names, Art precedes Arts. Within the Art group, Center precedes Centre. The complete name Brookside Art Center ends before the longer Center Annex and Center Archives names, so R1 comes before R4 and R6. Annex precedes Archives at n/r after A. R3 follows those Center names, and R2 follows every Art entry because it contains Arts. The correct order is R5-R1-R4-R6-R3-R2.

stem:
Arrange the records in ascending alphabetical order. R1, R2, and so on are fixed record labels, not answer-option letters. Ignore letter case. Each record is written Surname, Given names, with an optional title before the surname. Omit the titles Dr. and Ms. For surname comparison only, remove spaces and hyphens, retaining every surname letter. Compare normalized surnames letter by letter; if one is an exact prefix of another, the shorter comes first. If surnames tie, compare given names word by word, comparing letters within each word and placing the shorter exact word or complete-name prefix first.

R1: Dr. De Vera, Ana Marie
R2: De-Vera, Ana Maria Luisa
R3: Devera, Ana Mariel
R4: Ms. De Vera, Ana
R5: Deveras, Ana
R6: De Vera, Ana Maria

Which sequence gives the correct filing order?
explanation: After removing titles and joining surname spaces and hyphens, five surnames become Devera. Deveras is a longer exact prefix extension and follows that entire group. Within Devera, Ana alone comes first (R4). Ana Maria (R6) precedes its complete-name extension Ana Maria Luisa (R2). Both Maria entries precede Marie because a precedes e at the first difference in Maria/Marie; the extra word Luisa does not override that comparison. Marie then precedes its longer word extension Mariel (R1 before R3). R5 remains last because surname comparison takes priority over given names. The correct order is R4-R6-R2-R1-R3-R5.
